title: Measles: experts question vaccine coverage as study finds 24% of sampled children lack protective antibodies
excerpt: An IEDCR-led study found 24% of more than 300 sampled children had no protective measles antibodies. Experts want the vaccination drive and cold chain checked.

image.credit: File photo: CDC Global / Wikimedia Commons, CC BY 2.0

content:
Public health experts are questioning whether Bangladesh's measles vaccination campaigns are reaching children and working, after four rounds of vaccination in six months failed to stop infections and deaths, bdnews24.com's Bangla edition reported early on Wednesday (25 November).

According to Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) figures cited in the report, 1,361 people had died with measles or its symptoms by 24 November, 105 of them confirmed measles deaths. Almost all were children. Recorded cases reached 259,190. Dhaka division had the most deaths (631) and cases (177,038). DGHS counts only patients who reach hospital, so the real number is not known.

A study led by the Institute of Epidemiology, Disease Control and Research (IEDCR) of more than 300 children in three districts found that about 70% had developed measles antibodies after earlier rounds. Another 6% had borderline levels and 24% had no protective antibodies, IEDCR told bdnews24.com. An IEDCR official, speaking anonymously, said vaccine quality could be affected by problems anywhere from storage to injection. An Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) official said the sample was very small. Devlens has not seen the study.

Prof Mahmudur Rahman, chair of the National Verification Committee for measles-rubella elimination, said cases should have fallen at the reported coverage levels and that possible false reporting must be checked. Mushtuq Husain, former chief scientific officer at IEDCR, said EPI is short of about 20,000 field workers and that no proper micro-plan had been made, so remote and char areas could be missed. Vaccine expert Tajul Islam A Bari said about 80% of vaccines come from India and the whole supply chain should be checked.

The campaign launched on 26 September aimed to reach about 34 lakh missed children, after a gap of about 43 lakh was found between measles vaccination and vitamin A capsule numbers. DGHS data for 17 November showed more than 2.18 crore children vaccinated, leaving about 3 lakh, the report said. EPI assistant director Hasanul Mahmud said the cold chain is maintained, staff have been recruited in 27 districts, and internal checks on false reporting are under way.

DGHS director general Prof Prabhat Chandra Biswas said experts would be consulted once the target of about 2.26 crore is met. He said an international review of EPI found no specific problem but recommended filling staff gaps. Officials are considering what to do for infants under six months and children over 59 months, two groups now getting infected.

Why it matters

If coverage figures are overstated or vaccines lose potency, more rounds will not end the outbreak. NGO health workers who find missed children and refer sick ones are part of the response. Malnutrition, which weakens immune response, makes the gap more dangerous.

What to watch

Whether IEDCR publishes the antibody study, whether an independent coverage survey is ordered, and any decision to widen the age range for vaccination.
